scope: Standalone no_std journal primitive and external host consumer API tests; not kernel/runtime integration or product acceptance.
environment: Rust 1.90.0; PATH was prefixed with /tmp/nieuw-os-c-toolchain/bin and $HOME/.cargo/bin; CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/nieuw-os-system-journal-target. No dependencies.
implemented: Fixed-capacity ring with overwrite-oldest policy and saturating write/overwrite/drop/rejection counters.
Typed severity, subsystem, producer, event, correlation, and allowlisted metadata; no text or arbitrary byte payload field.
Per-producer Debug/Info rate limiting; Warning and higher bypass it.
Reader permits scoped to a journal identity and explicit subsystem allowlist; admin-only accounting snapshot.
Monotonic timestamp validation and optional wall timestamp.
limitations: The crate is deliberately standalone and is not in the root workspace; root manifest, kernel, SDK, and owned service code were not changed.
This is an in-memory host-tested primitive, not durable storage, native OS enforcement, a kernel panic recorder, or a connected system-wide consumer.
Typed metadata prevents free-form payload logging, but cannot prevent a trusted producer from deliberately encoding sensitive values into numeric fields.
No maturity rubric criterion was closed; product score remains unchanged.
blocked_next: SERVICE LIFECYCLE requires root/kernel/runtime paths. docs/WORK-QUEUE.md assigns shared root/runtime responsibility to REL4 and excludes new root writers; continue with CRASH DIAGNOSTICS only in a free independent crate, without kernel panic persistence.
